label: thm:main
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main}
Let $n\geq3$, and let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb S^n$ be closed, contain at
least two points, and satisfy \eqref{eq:dimension}. Then
$\Omega=\mathbb S^n\setminus\Lambda$ admits a complete metric
$g=u^{2/a}g_{\mathrm{rd}}$ of scalar curvature $n(n-1)$, with
$u\in C^\infty(\Omega)$ positive. Moreover, $u\in L^p(\mathbb S^n)$ and
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}u=\kappa u^p$ on the whole sphere in the sense of distributions.

body_md:
\label{thm:insertion}
There exists a universal $0<\eta_*\leq1$ with the following
property. For each fixed $0<\eta\leq\eta_*$ and each choice of data $(U_0,D,K)$ as above, every such family with sufficiently small
$\max_i r_i$ and $Q$ admits a marked nondegenerate finite-ended
solution $U_1$ with singular set $F\cup\{y_i\}$.
On $D\setminus\bigcup_i B(y_i,\rho_i)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:core-lower}
 U_1\geq c\left(
 U_0+\sum_i\frac{A_i}{(\rho_i^2+|x-y_i|^2)^a}
 \right),
\end{equation}
where $c>0$ depends only on the universal data and $\eta$.
By decreasing the radius and coefficient bounds, $u_1$ can be
made arbitrarily close to $u_0$ in any prescribed finite
collection of $C^m$ norms on compact subsets of
$\mathbb S^n\setminus(F\cup K)$, while the old neck and phase
parameters remain in any prescribed neighborhood of their
original values.

label: pot:pointwise
title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\gamma=(a-\beta)/a\in(0,1)$ and
$D_j(x)=(\rho_j^2+|x-y_j|^2)^{1/2}$.  We first prove
\begin{equation}\label{pot:pointwise}
 h(x)^p\le C\eta^{a+2}\nu^{\gamma-2}
       \sum_j r_j^{a+\gamma}D_j(x)^{-n-\gamma}.
\end{equation}
Suppose $x$ is outside every original ball, so that
$d_j=|x-y_j|\ge r_j$, and write
$$
 S=\sum_j r_j^ad_j^{-2a},\qquad
 T=\sum_j r_j^{a+\gamma}d_j^{-n-\gamma}.
$$
Since $n=2a+2$ and $a\gamma+\beta=a$,
$$
 r_j^ad_j^{-2a}
 =\bigl(r_j^{a+\gamma}d_j^{-n-\gamma}\bigr)^{a/(a+1)}
   \bigl(r_j^\beta d_j^{a-\beta}\bigr)^{1/(a+1)}.
$$
H\"older's inequality and packing give, for $R>0$,
$$
 \sum_{d_j\le R}r_j^ad_j^{-2a}
 \le T^{a/(a+1)}
      \left(\sum_{d_j\le R}r_j^\beta d_j^{a-\beta}\right)^{1/(a+1)}
 \le C(RT)^{a/(a+1)}.
$$
On a shell $2^kR<d_j\le2^{k+1}R$, all $r_j$ are at most
$2^{k+1}R$, and hence
$$
 \sum r_j^a\le(2^{k+1}R)^{a-\beta}\sum r_j^\beta
 \le C(2^kR)^a.
$$
The near--far decomposition, as in \cite{Hedberg1972}, therefore gives
$$
 S\le C(RT)^{a/(a+1)}+CR^{-a}.
$$
If the family is nonempty, take $R=T^{-1/(a+2)}$ to obtain
$S^p\le CT$.  Since $d_j\le D_j\le\sqrt2d_j$ and
$\nu^{\gamma-2}\ge1$, this proves \eqref{pot:pointwise} outside
the original balls.  The empty family is immediate.

If $x\in B(y_i,r_i)$, disjointness permits the same argument
for $H_i$.  For the remaining term, $D_i\ge\nu r_i$ and
$\gamma<2$ imply
$$
 h_i^p
 =2^{a+2}\eta^{a+2}r_i^{a+2}D_i^{-n-2}
 \le C\eta^{a+2}\nu^{\gamma-2}
          r_i^{a+\gamma}D_i^{-n-\gamma}.
$$
Together with $(h_i+H_i)^p\le2^{p-1}(h_i^p+H_i^p)$, this
proves \eqref{pot:pointwise} everywhere.

For $f_\rho(t)=(\rho^2+t^2)^{-(n+\gamma)/2}$, the radial
Newtonian formula bounds $\mathcal I_2f_\rho(D)$ by
$C\rho^{2-n-\gamma}$ for $D\le\rho$, and by
$C\rho^{-\gamma}D^{2-n}$ for $D\ge\rho$. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{pot:convolution}
 \mathcal I_2\bigl((\rho^2+|\cdot-y|^2)^{-(n+\gamma)/2}\bigr)(x)
 \le C\rho^{-\gamma}(\rho^2+|x-y|^2)^{-a}.
\end{equation}
Applying this to \eqref{pot:pointwise}, using $\rho_j=\nu r_j$,
yields
$$
 \mathcal I_2(h^p)
 \le C\eta^{a+2}\nu^{-2}
       \sum_jr_j^a(\rho_j^2+|x-y_j|^2)^{-a}
 =C\delta h.
$$
Multiplying \eqref{pot:endpointineq} by $|x|^{n-2}$,
letting $x$ tend to infinity along a ray, and applying Fatou's
lemma gives $\gamma_n\int h^p\le C\delta Q$, since
$|x|^{n-2}h(x)\to Q$. This proves \eqref{pot:mass}, including
integrability.

label: pot:taildensity
title: Proof
body_md:
Using the identity
$h_i=(\lambda_i/\rho_i)^a b_{\rho_i,y_i}$,
the bubble equation, and decay at infinity, we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{pot:taildensity}
 -\Delta h_i=\kappa\delta^{-1}h_i^p>0,
 \qquad h_i=\kappa\delta^{-1}\mathcal I_2(h_i^p),
\end{equation}
with $h_i^p\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$.
For $K(x,z)=\gamma_n|x-z|^{2-n}$, the standard three-kernel
inequality (see \cite[equations~(1.6) and~(3.1)]{KaltonVerbitsky1999}) is
\begin{equation}\label{pot:3G}
 K(x,z)K(z,y)
 \le C_nK(x,y)\bigl(K(x,z)+K(z,y)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Integrating against $V(z)\,\mathrm d z\,\mathrm d\mu(y)$ and using Tonelli's
theorem gives
$$
 \mathcal I_2(VW)(x)
 \le C_n\int K(x,y)
     \bigl(\mathcal I_2V(x)+\mathcal I_2V(y)\bigr)\,\mathrm d\mu(y)
 \le C_nLW(x).
$$

title: Proof
body_md:
In a flat chart about each puncture, the Euclidean conformal factor
is a nonnegative $C^2$ solution of $-\Delta U=\kappa U^p$.
Since $p=(n+2)/(n-2)>n/(n-2)$, \cite[Lemma~2.1]{CGS1989}
gives local $L^p$ integrability and the distributional equation
across the puncture.  Conformal covariance therefore yields
$u_0\in L^p(\mathbb S^n)$ and \eqref{eq:finite-distribution}.

The stereographic pole is regular, so $U_0=O(|x|^{2-n})$ and
$U_0^p=O(|x|^{-n-2})$ at infinity.  Thus $U_0^p\in L^1(\mathbb R^n)$,
and the standard near--far estimate gives
$\mathcal I_2(U_0^p)=O(|x|^{2-n})$.  Conformal covariance also
gives $-\Delta U_0=\kappa U_0^p$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^n)$.
Hence $U_0-\kappa\mathcal I_2(U_0^p)$ is distributionally
harmonic on all of $\mathbb R^n$ and tends to zero at infinity.
Weyl's lemma and Liouville's theorem prove \eqref{pot:oldnewton};
\eqref{pot:singlemultiplier} then gives \eqref{pot:oldmultiplier}.

label: pot:background
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{pot:background}
Packing and disjointness imply
\begin{equation}\label{pot:interactionrow}
 \sup_i\sum_{j\ne i}
       \left(\frac{r_ir_j}{|y_i-y_j|^2}\right)^a\le C.
\end{equation}
Suppose the centers lie in a fixed compact subset of the regular
domain of $U_0$, and write
$$
 B_i=U_0(y_i)+\sum_{j\ne i}b_{\lambda_j,y_j}(y_i).
$$
For each finite derivative order $m_0$, the maximal radius can
be chosen sufficiently small, depending on $U_0$, the compact
set, and $\eta$, so that
\begin{align}
 B_ir_i^a&\le C\eta^a,\label{pot:backgroundsize}\\
 r_i^m\left|D^m\left(U_0+\sum_{j\ne i}b_{\lambda_j,y_j}\right)(y_i)\right|
 &\le C_mB_i\quad(0\le m\le m_0),
 \label{pot:backgroundjets}\\
 A_iB_i&\le C\eta^{2a},\qquad
 \frac{B_i\rho_i^{2a}}{A_i}\le C\nu^{2a}.
 \label{pot:backgroundconsequences}
\end{align}
The constants are independent of the old solution.

title: Proof
body_md:
Disjointness gives $d_{ij}=|y_i-y_j|\ge r_i+r_j$.
The far-field shell estimate in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{pot:endpoint}, applied at $y_i$ with $R=r_i$
and the $i$th ball omitted, proves \eqref{pot:interactionrow}.
Hence the other bubbles contribute at most $C\eta^ar_i^{-a}$
to $B_i$.
Choose the maximal radius so that
$\sup U_0\,r_i^a\le\eta^a$ on the compact set.  This gives
\eqref{pot:backgroundsize}.

For $j\ne i$,
$$
 |D^mb_{\lambda_j,y_j}(y_i)|
 \le C_mb_{\lambda_j,y_j}(y_i)d_{ij}^{-m}.
$$
Since $r_i\le d_{ij}$, summing gives the bubble contribution
to \eqref{pot:backgroundjets}.  The old factor has bounded
relative derivatives on the fixed compact neighborhood, so
reducing the maximal radius gives the same estimate for it.
Finally, insert $A_i=2^a\eta^ar_i^a$ and $\rho_i=\nu r_i$
into \eqref{pot:backgroundsize} to obtain
\eqref{pot:backgroundconsequences}.

label: in:radial-integrals
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $w_\varepsilon$ be the periodic profile normalized by
$w_\varepsilon(0)=\varepsilon$ and $w_\varepsilon'(0)=0$; write
$T=T(\varepsilon)$ and $M=M(\varepsilon)$ for its period and maximum.
On the increasing half-period,
$$
 (w_\varepsilon')^2=D_\varepsilon(w_\varepsilon),\qquad
 D_\varepsilon(z)
  =a^2\bigl(z^2-\varepsilon^2-z^{q+2}+\varepsilon^{q+2}\bigr).
$$
Fix a small $c=c(n)>0$ and split the energy integral into
$[\varepsilon,2\varepsilon]$, $[2\varepsilon,c]$, and $[c,M]$.
In the first interval the substitution $z=\varepsilon Z$ gives
$\varepsilon^{-2}D_\varepsilon(\varepsilon Z)\asymp Z^2-1$.
In the middle interval $D_\varepsilon(z)\asymp z^2$. In the last,
$M\to1$ and $|D_\varepsilon'(M)|$ is bounded below; hence the
square-root singularity at $M$ is uniformly integrable. These estimates
give
\begin{equation}\label{in:radial-integrals}
 \int_0^t w_\varepsilon^{q+2}(\tau)\,\mathrm d\tau
       \leq Cw_\varepsilon^{q+2}(t),\qquad
 \int_0^{T/2}w_\varepsilon^q(\tau)\,\mathrm d\tau\leq C
       \quad(0\leq t\leq T/2).
\end{equation}

Set $j=\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon w_\varepsilon$ and
$h=j/w_\varepsilon$. The variational equation gives
$$
 (w_\varepsilon^2h')'
   =-\kappa q w_\varepsilon^{q+2}h,\qquad h(0)=1,\quad h'(0)=0.
$$
By \eqref{in:radial-integrals},
$$
 |h'(t)|\leq Cw_\varepsilon^q(t)
               \sup_{0\leq\tau\leq t}|h(\tau)|.
$$
Gronwall's inequality therefore bounds $h$ and $h'$ uniformly on the
increasing half-period. Since $|w_\varepsilon'|\leq aw_\varepsilon$,
$$
 |\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon w_\varepsilon|
  +|\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon w_\varepsilon'|
       \leq Cw_\varepsilon.
$$
At the maximum, $|w_\varepsilon''(T/2)|$ is uniformly positive.
Differentiating $w_\varepsilon'(T/2)=0$ gives
$|\varepsilon T_\varepsilon|\leq C$. Differentiation of the reflection
identity $w_\varepsilon(t)=w_\varepsilon(T-t)$ extends the relative
bound to the first full period.

The cutoff data satisfy
$$
\begin{aligned}
 v_0:=v_B(0)&\asymp s^a,& |E|/v_0^2&\leq C\vartheta_B,\\
 |\partial_bv_0|/v_0&\leq C\vartheta_B,&
 v_B'(0)/v_0&=a(1+O(s^2+\vartheta_B)).
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus the cutoff lies in the increasing middle interval. If
$w_\varepsilon(\tau_B)=v_0$ with $0<\tau_B<T/2$, then
$w_\varepsilon'(\tau_B)\asymp av_0$ and
$$
 (\tau_B)_b
  =\frac{\partial_bv_0-\varepsilon_b
                   \partial_\varepsilon w_\varepsilon(\tau_B)}
          {w_\varepsilon'(\tau_B)},\qquad |(\tau_B)_b|\leq C.
$$
Also $|T_b|\leq C$, since $|\varepsilon_b|\leq C\varepsilon$.
Now $v_B(t)=w_\varepsilon(t+\tau_B)$. In the $k$th period,
differentiating periodicity introduces the term $-kT_bw_\varepsilon'$;
this is the familiar linear growth of the neck-variation Jacobi field
\cite[Section~5, Lemma~3]{MP1999}; \cite[Section~II]{MPU1996}.
The energy integral on $[c/2,c]$ gives
$T\geq2a^{-1}\log2$ for small $\varepsilon$, so $k\leq C(1+t)$, proving
\eqref{in:radial-loss} for $m=0,1$. The equation and its variational
equation give the higher derivatives; throughout,
$|v_B^{(m)}|\leq C_mv_B$ for each fixed $m$.

Finally, negative energy gives $|v_B'|\leq av_B$ and $v_B\leq1$.
Hence $v_B(t)\leq Cs^ae^{at}$ and
$r^2Q_B=\kappa p v_B^q\leq C\min\{1,s^2e^{2t}\}$.
The parameter estimate follows from \eqref{in:radial-loss}.
One spatial derivative introduces $r^{-1}$, so these pointwise
estimates also give the scaled H\"older bounds.

label: in:fixed-point
title: Proof
body_md:
Write $U=\mathcal T_{\boldsymbol z}U_B$, $Q_U=\kappa pU^q$,
$L_U=\Delta+Q_U$, and let $G_U$ be its inverse from
\eqref{in:inverse}. Set
$$
 N_U(Z)=\kappa\bigl((U+Z)^p-U^p-pU^qZ\bigr).
$$
The equation for the correction is
\begin{equation}\label{in:fixed-point}
 W=-G_U\bigl(Q_UH_\phi+N_U(H_\phi+W)\bigr).
\end{equation}
On the ball $\|W\|_{X_{\mu_3}}\leq C_0s^{2-\mu_3}\|\phi\|$,
the lower bound $U\geq c\varepsilon r^{-a}$ and uniform scaled
derivative bounds for $U$ give
$$
 |(H_\phi+W)/U|_{2,\theta;r}
  \leq C\|\phi\|\rho^a/\varepsilon
  \leq C\sqrt{\vartheta_*}\|\psi\|=: \omega.
$$
For $\omega<1/2$, Taylor's formula on $[1-\omega,1+\omega]$ gives,
for every $p>1$,
$$
 |N_U(Z)|\leq C\omega Q_U|Z|,\qquad
 |D_ZN_U(Z)|\leq C\omega Q_U,
$$
with the corresponding scaled H\"older estimates. In particular,
$$
 \|N_U(H_\phi+W)\|_{Y_\mu}
  \leq C\omega\bigl(\|Q_UH_\phi\|_{Y_\mu}
                        +\|W\|_{X_\mu}\bigr).
$$
Taking $\omega$ small relative to the three inverse bounds makes
\eqref{in:fixed-point} a contraction by \eqref{in:h-forcing},
proving \eqref{in:w-size} and positivity. The same contraction works
at each weaker weight in the common ball of radius
$C_0s^{2-\mu_3}\|\phi\|$, since $s^{2-\mu}\leq s^{2-\mu_3}$;
uniqueness identifies these solutions.

For fixed $Z$ in the relative neighborhood above,
\begin{equation}\label{in:nonlinear-background}
 |\partial_bN_U(Z)|
  \leq C(1+t)\omega Q_U|Z|,
\end{equation}
with its scaled H\"older version. This follows by differentiating
Taylor's formula and using \eqref{in:radial-loss}. A
$\boldsymbol c$ derivative has $r/\rho$ in place of $1+t$.
The positive neighborhood can be chosen uniformly for nearby
parameters, because $\varepsilon^2\asymp AB$ and $B/B_*$ stays in a
fixed compact interval.

We first treat $b$. Keep $\boldsymbol c,\psi$ fixed and set
$$
 U^{(b)}=\mathcal T_{\boldsymbol z}U_{B_*e^b},\qquad
 Q^{(b)}=\kappa p(U^{(b)})^q,\qquad
 L^{(b)}=\Delta+Q^{(b)}.
$$
Write $W_b=W(b,\boldsymbol c,\psi)$, $W_h=W(b+h,\boldsymbol c,\psi)$,
$Z_h=H_\phi+W_h$, and $Z=H_\phi+W_b$. Set
$$
 C_h=\int_0^1D_ZN_{U^{(b)}}\bigl(Z+\tau(Z_h-Z)\bigr)\,\mathrm d\tau.
$$
Its multiplier norm $X_\mu\to Y_\mu$ is at most $C\omega$.
Subtracting the equations gives
\begin{equation}\label{in:parameter-difference}
\begin{aligned}
 (L^{(b)}+C_h)(W_h-W_b)
  &=-(Q^{(b+h)}-Q^{(b)})(H_\phi+W_h)\\
  &\quad-\bigl(N_{U^{(b+h)}}(Z_h)-N_{U^{(b)}}(Z_h)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
All three realizations of $L^{(b)}+C_h$ are uniformly invertible by a
Neumann series. To estimate the source, put $d=\mu_3-\mu_2$. The
potential envelope gives
$$
 \sup_{t\geq0}(1+t)e^{-dt}\min\{1,s^2e^{2t}\}
       \leq C_d(1+\ell_s)s^d.
$$
Indeed, write $t=\ell_s-u$ before the transition and $t=\ell_s+u$ after it.
The two factors to bound are respectively
$(1+\ell_s)s^de^{-(2-d)u}$ and
$s^d(1+\ell_s+u)e^{-du}$.
Thus
$$
 \|(\partial_bQ_U)W_h\|_{Y_{\mu_2}}
   \leq C(1+\ell_s)s^{\mu_3-\mu_2}\|W_h\|_{X_{\mu_3}}
   \leq C(1+\ell_s)s^{2-\mu_2}\|\phi\|.
$$
For the harmonic term use \eqref{in:h-forcing-derivative}; for the
nonlinear difference use \eqref{in:nonlinear-background} and the
same multiplier estimate. Integration along the parameter interval
in \eqref{in:parameter-difference} yields local Lipschitz continuity
into $X_{\mu_2}$ and
$$
 \left\|(W_h-W_b)/h\right\|_{X_{\mu_2}}
     \leq C(1+\ell_s)s^{2-\mu_2}B_*\|\psi\|_{C^{2,\theta}}.
$$

To obtain differentiability, divide
\eqref{in:parameter-difference} by $h$. On each compact annulus the
source converges in $C^{0,\theta}$ to
$$
 F_b=-(\partial_bQ^{(b)})(H_\phi+W_b)
       -\partial_bN_{U^{(b)}}(H_\phi+W_b),
$$
where the last derivative holds its argument fixed. The tails are
uniformly small in $Y_{\mu_1}$: the correction terms are bounded by
$(1+t)e^{-(\mu_3-\mu_1)t}$ and the harmonic terms by their degree-two
decay. Also $C_h\to D_ZN_{U^{(b)}}(Z)$ on compact annuli; acting on the
bounded $X_{\mu_2}$ difference quotients, its tails gain
$e^{-(\mu_2-\mu_1)t}$. Applying the fixed inverse at $\mu_1$ proves
convergence of the difference quotients to the unique solution of
\begin{equation}\label{in:parameter-derivative}
 \bigl(L_U+D_ZN_U(Z)\bigr)\partial_bW
  =-(\partial_bQ_U)(H_\phi+W)-\partial_bN_U(Z),
 \qquad Z=H_\phi+W.
\end{equation}
In particular the coefficient derivative acts on $W$ as well as on
$H_\phi$. The source belongs to $Y_{\mu_2}$; compatibility of inverses
gives \eqref{in:w-b}. Comparing this equation at nearby parameters,
using convergence on compact annuli and the same tail bounds, proves
continuity of $\partial_bW$ into $X_{\mu_1}$.

For $\boldsymbol c$, the additional factor $r/\rho$ makes coefficient
differentiation bounded on a single weighted space. The same
subtraction argument at $\mu_3$ gives \eqref{in:w-c}. Differentiation
in $\psi$ gives
$$
 \bigl(L_U+D_ZN_U(Z)\bigr)D_\psi W[\dot\psi]
   =-\bigl(Q_U+D_ZN_U(Z)\bigr)H_{B_*\dot\psi},
$$
which proves \eqref{in:w-psi}. These comparison equations give joint
continuity of the derivatives into $X_{\mu_1}$.

Restriction to the outer annulus is bounded from $X_{\mu_1}$ to
$C^{2,\theta}$, and $\rho\partial_r$ maps its trace to
$C^{1,\theta}$. Since $\Pi_{\mathrm{hi}}W|_{r=\rho}=0$, the claimed
boundary error is exactly
$\mathcal E=B_*^{-1}\Pi_{\mathrm{hi}}\rho\partial_rW|_{r=\rho}$.
The estimates and their parameter versions follow from the corresponding
bounds for $W$.

label: old:common-complement
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{old:common-complement}
The old cross sections can be chosen so that the disjoint union $E$
of the old tails has the following properties. Its Dirichlet
operator on the pure decaying space is injective and has index $-m$.
After adjoining $\mathcal W$ it is surjective, with an $m$-dimensional
kernel whose radial coefficient image $N_{\rm tail}$ is a $m$-plane in
$\mathcal W$. There is a single $m$-plane $\mathcal W'$ complementary
to both $Z$ and $N_{\rm tail}$. The whole old operator and the tail Dirichlet operator restricted to decay plus $\mathcal W'$ are
isomorphisms for every $0<d\leq d_+$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First consider an exact radial Delaunay half-cylinder. Its conjugated
Jacobi equation is
$$
 w_{tt}+\Delta_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}w-a^2w+\kappa p v_\epsilon^{p-1}w=0.
$$
The radial equation has two independent Jacobi fields with Floquet
multiplier one; one may grow linearly in $t$. Neither decays. The decaying first spherical field
$e^{-t}(av_\epsilon-v_\epsilon')$ has a strictly positive periodic
factor, hence nonzero boundary trace. For degrees at least two,
$$
 a^2+2n-\kappa p v_\epsilon^{p-1}\geq a+2>0.
$$
Integration by parts on the half-cylinder therefore excludes a
decaying field of spherical degree at least two with zero Dirichlet trace. Boundary terms at
infinity vanish by the decay and local elliptic estimates.

Radial variation of constants, the explicit first spherical modes,
and the coercive estimate for degrees at least two give the
inhomogeneous bounds. Local elliptic estimates then give the required
H\"older regularity. In the radial
sector decay imposes one compatibility condition on the source with
zero trace; adjoining the two neutral fields removes that condition
and leaves one kernel direction. Every nonradial decaying Dirichlet problem is invertible. Thus each
end has index $-1$ before extension, and contributes one kernel
direction after the surjective radial extension.

For the original tails the difference from the model operator is
exponentially small after the cuts are moved out. The preceding
estimates and a Neumann series preserve pure-decay injectivity and
extended surjectivity. Index stability gives kernel dimension $m$.
A kernel field with zero radial coefficients is pure decaying, so its
coefficient map is injective. Its image is $N_{\rm tail}$.

Choose $\mathcal W'$ in the intersection of the two open dense
sets of $m$-planes complementary to $Z$ and $N_{\rm tail}$.
Removing the respective kernel by this common complement gives both
isomorphisms. Changing $d$ within $(0,d_+]$ crosses no
indicial exponent and stays below the coefficient decay rate, so the
coefficient planes and the choice of complement are unchanged.
The Sobolev to H\"older argument above gives the asserted realizations.

\label{old:nonlinear-graph}\label{old:graph}
For full boundary increments $\gamma\in C^{2,\theta}(\Sigma)$ near
zero, the eliminated tails and cap have a unique positive solution in a
fixed neighborhood of the old solution in the period-aligned coordinates,
with old radial parameter increment in $\mathcal W'$. Its physical
Neumann trace has the form
\begin{equation}\label{old:graph-expansion}
\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal N_{\mathrm{old}}(\gamma)&=\mathcal N_{\mathrm{old}}(0)+T\gamma+\mathcal E(\gamma),\\
 \|\mathcal E(\gamma)\|_{C^{1,\theta}}
       &\leq C_{\rm old}\|\gamma\|_{C^{2,\theta}}^2,\\
 \|D\mathcal E(\gamma)\|
       &\leq C_{\rm old}\|\gamma\|_{C^{2,\theta}}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
This is a $C^2$ boundary map. At a sufficiently small boundary
increment its derivative represents every Jacobi field on the
eliminated pieces whose radial parameter derivative belongs to
$\mathcal W'$ and whose physical remainder has decay $d_-$. In
particular it represents every Jacobi field with zero radial coefficients and positive
exponential decay there.

label: old:pulled-operator
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $w=(\epsilon_j-\epsilon_j^0,\phi_j-\phi_j^0)_j\in\mathcal W'$.
Choose an absolute cylindrical factor $A_w$ equal to the old solution
on a boundary collar and to the new radial model plus the fixed old
decaying remainder far out.
Use $t=F_w(s)$, equal to the identity on that collar and to
$c_j(w)s+b_j(w)$ far out on the $j$th end, where
$$
 c_j(w)=T(\epsilon_j)/T(\epsilon_j^0).
$$
Choose $b_j$ smoothly and place the transition on a fixed compact
interval separated from the collar.
The pulled operator on $V(s,\omega)$ is
\begin{equation}\label{old:pulled-operator}
 F_s^{-2}V_{ss}-F_{ss}F_s^{-3}V_s+
 \Delta_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}V-a^2V+\kappa V^p.
\end{equation}
With $z_\epsilon(\vartheta)=v_\epsilon(T(\epsilon)\vartheta/(2\pi))$,
the far-out leading profile is
$$
 z_{\epsilon_j}\left(\frac{2\pi s}{T(\epsilon_j^0)}+
              \frac{2\pi(b_j+\phi_j)}{T(\epsilon_j)}\right).
$$
It solves the pulled equation there and has bounded parameter
derivatives on the fixed period circle near each positive old neck.

Let $H\gamma$ be a bounded cylindrical extension supported in the
collar where $F_w$ is the identity, with flat-section trace
$r^a\gamma$ and the fixed conformal conversion included.
Write $V=A_w\circ F_w+H\gamma+e$, with
$e\in\mathcal C_{d_+,0}^{2,\theta}$; the subscript $0$ denotes zero
full boundary trace.
The pulled residual $\mathcal F(e,w,\gamma)$ is $C^2$ into the
weighted source space.
Indeed, the variable remainder $e$ is never composed with $F_w$,
so parameter differentiation requires no derivatives beyond $e_{ss}$.
Only the fixed smooth old remainder is composed with $F_w$; its first
two parameter derivatives acquire polynomial factors of degree at most
two, absorbed by the strict decay gap in \eqref{old:weights} after
shrinking the parameter neighborhood. The fixed positive profiles
preserve positivity nearby.
At the base point, the derivative in $(e,w)$ is the physical Dirichlet
Jacobi operator, up to an invertible triangular change of remainder:
the coordinate derivative of the base residual vanishes.
Lemma~\ref{old:common-complement} therefore makes it an isomorphism.
The implicit function theorem gives a positive $C^2$ solution graph,
and the fixed collar coordinates make its Neumann trace a bounded
linear observation. Taylor's theorem gives \eqref{old:graph-expansion}.

For the physical tangent identification, let $c_{\min}$ and
$c_{\max}$ bound the slopes $c_j(w)$ throughout a smaller neighborhood,
and arrange
$$
 c_{\max}d_-<d_+,\qquad
 c_{\min}\min\{1,\gamma_{\rm old}\}>d_+,\qquad
 0<\widetilde d<\min\{d_+,c_{\min}d_-\}.
$$
Fix $\widetilde d$ on this neighborhood.
Lemma~\ref{old:common-complement} gives the base isomorphism at
this weight with the same complement.
At a current graph point $(e_*,w_*,\gamma_*)$, the derivative extends to
$$
 \mathcal A_*:
 \mathcal C_{\widetilde d,0}^{2,\theta}\oplus\mathcal W'
 \longrightarrow\mathcal C_{\widetilde d}^{0,\theta}.
$$
Period alignment keeps the leading profiles and principal coefficients
uniformly close to their base values. The parameter derivatives of the
fixed old remainder decay faster than $d_+$, and the terms involving
$e_*$ decay at $d_+$, so the finite-dimensional derivatives are close
in the $\widetilde d$ source norm as well.
Thus $\mathcal A_*$ is a small perturbation of the base isomorphism
and remains invertible.
Graph derivatives have physical remainders of decay $d_-$: differentiation
at fixed physical $t$ adds at most a factor $1+t$ to the solved
remainder, while $d_+/c_{\max}>d_-$.

Let $J$ be a physical Jacobi field with the stated decay and radial
coefficients in $\mathcal W'$. Subtract the graph derivative with its
full Dirichlet trace, obtaining a zero-trace field $J^0$ with
$h=r^aJ^0$ and radial coefficient vector $\zeta\in\mathcal W'$.
On the far tails,
$$
 h(t)=\partial_w v_{w_*}(t)\zeta+h_{\rm dec}(t),
 \qquad h_{\rm dec}\in\mathcal C_{d_-}^{2,\theta},
$$
where $v_w$ is the physical leading radial model.
Set $F=F_{w_*}$ and $\dot F_\zeta=D_wF_{w_*}\zeta$.
For the current physical factor $V_{\rm phys}$, differentiating
$V_{\rm phys}\circ F=A_{w_*}\circ F+H\gamma_*+e_*$ gives the
period-aligned remainder derivative
$$
 \widehat e_{J^0}
 =h\circ F-(\partial_w A_{w_*})\circ F\,\zeta
   +\frac{\dot F_\zeta}{F_s}\,\partial_s e_* .
$$
The collar extension has zero derivative for this difference field.
Far out, $\partial_w A_{w_*}=\partial_wv_{w_*}$, so the first two
terms reduce to $h_{\rm dec}\circ F$, with decay at least
$c_{\min}d_-$; the last is $O((1+s)e^{-d_+s})$ in
$C^{2,\theta}$ on unit strips.
For this last assertion, $\dot F_\zeta$ is supported away from the
boundary collar, where the equation has smooth coefficients and no
collar forcing. Interior Schauder estimates and differentiation of the
equation give the additional spatial derivatives of $e_*$ with the
same decay, without extra boundary regularity of $\gamma_*$.
Near the boundary, $F$ is the identity, $\dot F_\zeta=0$, and
$A_w$ is independent of $w$. Hence
$\widehat e_{J^0}\in\mathcal C_{\widetilde d,0}^{2,\theta}$.
Differentiation at zero residual yields
$$
 \mathcal A_*(\widehat e_{J^0},\zeta)=0.
$$
Invertibility forces both entries to vanish, so $J^0=0$.
This proves the stated tangent identification. Marked fields have zero
radial coefficients and decay at every rate below the first nonradial
exponent $1$, so they are included; the cap uses compact Dirichlet
uniqueness.

label: old:perforated-inverse
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{old:perforated-inverse}\label{old:inverse}
For sufficiently small $c_N$ the problem
\begin{equation}\label{old:linear-boundary-problem}
 L_0v=f\text{ in }D_N,\qquad v=g\text{ on }\Gamma_N,
 \qquad \partial_{\mathbf n} v-T(v|_\Sigma)=r\text{ on }\Sigma
\end{equation}
has a unique solution. For every fixed $U\Subset D$ containing all
new balls its zero-new-trace source inverse $G_N^0$ has a kernel
satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{old:green-kernel}
 |G_N^0(x,z)|\leq C_n|x-z|^{2-n}+C_{\rm old},
 \qquad x,z\in U\cap D_N.
\end{equation}
If the source is supported in $U$ and separated from a fixed old
collar, the $C^{2,\theta}$ norm of the solution on that collar is
at most $C_{\rm old}\|f\|_{L^1}$. Smooth interface forcing has
a uniformly bounded $C^0$ response on $U\cap D_N$, with uniform
scaled local $C^{2,\theta}$ estimates on the new collars and interior
patches. Ordinary $C^k$ estimates hold on compact subsets staying
a fixed positive distance from the holes. All these constants are
independent of the number of holes and their radius ratios.

title: Proof
body_md:
Keep the old sections fixed and choose a sufficiently small regular cap
with invertible Dirichlet Jacobi operator.
An arbitrarily small outward change of its outer radius makes the full Dirichlet
operator on $D$ invertible: strict domain monotonicity, by min--max and
unique continuation \cite{Aronszajn1957}, leaves only countably many
exceptional radii. The cap radius is chosen within the preceding
working-core convention, preserving $D\supset D_{\rm pre}$.

Put $B_{D,N}=-\Delta-V_0$ with full Dirichlet data. Choose
$\chi_i=1$ on $B(y_i,\rho_i)$, supported in $B(y_i,2\rho_i)$, with
$\int|\nabla\chi_i|^2\leq C_n\rho_i^{n-2}$, in a fixed neighborhood
separated from $\Sigma$. Their supports are disjoint
because $2\rho_i+2\rho_j<r_i+r_j$. For $\chi=\sum_i\chi_i$,
multiplication by $1-\chi$ changes each fixed smooth trial function by
$O(c_N^{1/2})$ in $H^1$; the support volume is at most
$C_n\rho_{\max}^2c_N$. Min--max and domain monotonicity therefore give
convergence of the fixed eigenvalues and a uniform gap about zero,
as in the capacitary perturbation method of \cite{RauchTaylor1975}.
The uniformly coercive shifted form, with
$c_{\rm shift}>\|V_0\|_\infty+1$, and spectral calculus give a uniform
$H^{-1}\to H^1$ inverse bound.

For sufficiently small fixed $t_0>0$, use the signed-resolvent identity
$$
 B_{D,N}^{-1}=\int_0^{t_0}e^{-tB_{D,N}}\,\mathrm d t+
 e^{-t_0B_{D,N}/2}B_{D,N}^{-1}e^{-t_0B_{D,N}/2}.
$$
Dirichlet heat-kernel domination \cite[Chapters~1 and~3]{Davies1989}
bounds the first kernel by $C_n|x-z|^{2-n}$, choosing
$e^{t_0\|V_0\|_\infty}\leq e$. The gap and the Gaussian $L^2$ row
bounds make the second kernel bounded by $C_{\rm old}$; no positivity
of the resolvent is required.

Let $D_N^\Sigma$ be the core Dirichlet-to-Neumann map with zero new
trace. The no-hole Poisson solution $u_0$ for
$\varphi\in H^{1/2}(\Sigma)$ has uniformly bounded interior jets near
the holes. Correcting $(1-\chi)u_0$ by the preceding inverse gives,
after zero extension across the holes,
$$
 \|u_N-u_0\|_{H^1(D)}
 \leq C_{\rm old}\|\chi u_0\|_{H^1(D)}
 \leq C_{\rm old}c_N^{1/2}\|\varphi\|_{H^{1/2}(\Sigma)}.
$$
The difference is homogeneous with zero trace on a fixed collar of
$\Sigma$, so boundary regularity gives, for every fixed $s$,
$$
 \|D_N^\Sigma-D_0^\Sigma\|_{H^{1/2}(\Sigma)\to H^s(\Sigma)}
 \leq C_{{\rm old},s}c_N^{1/2}.
$$

Weighted regularity extends $T:H^{1/2}\to H^{-1/2}$. Remote-end
responses are smoothing, and changing $\mathcal W'$ adds finite-rank
smooth terms. The local calculus \cite[Theorems~11.17--11.18]{Grubb2009}
therefore gives $D_0^\Sigma-T$ principal symbol $2|\xi|$ and index
zero by deformation to $2(1-\Delta_\Sigma)^{1/2}$. Its kernel glues
to a whole old Jacobi field with coefficients
in $\mathcal W'$, excluded by Lemma~\ref{old:common-complement}.
Thus $D_N^\Sigma-T$ remains uniformly invertible by the smoothing
perturbation, without selfadjointness of $T$.

Solve the full Dirichlet problem and correct its old normal trace
using $(D_N^\Sigma-T)^{-1}$ and the old-boundary Poisson operator.
A fixed-collar extension of smooth old data and the separated
Dirichlet kernel bound give this Poisson operator a uniform bound on
$U$. For a source pole in $U$, fixed-collar estimates bound its old
normal trace and hence its interface correction by $C_{\rm old}$.
This proves \eqref{old:green-kernel}; differentiation on fixed collars
gives the stated separated-source and interface estimates.
Finally, the new collars are disjoint fixed-shape annuli after
rescaling, with uniformly small smooth potential
$\rho_i^2V_0(y_i+\rho_i\cdot)$. Local boundary and interior estimates
\cite[Chapters~6 and~8]{GT2001} therefore have constants independent
of $N$ and all radius ratios.

label: old:poisson
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First solve with new data $g$ and old data zero using the selfadjoint
compact full Dirichlet inverse. For $x\notin B(y_i,2\rho_i)$, its
Green kernel, as a function of the source variable $z$, has zero trace
and solves the homogeneous equation on
$B(y_i,3\rho_i/2)\setminus\overline{B(y_i,\rho_i)}$.
Rescaled boundary gradient estimates and the Dirichlet kernel bound give
$$
 |\partial_{\mathbf n_z}G_{D,N}(x,z)|
 \leq C\rho_i^{-1}(|x-y_i|^{2-n}+C_{\rm old}),
 \qquad z\in\partial B(y_i,\rho_i).
$$
Integration over the sphere contributes $b_i\rho_i^{n-2}$.
On doubled new collars, the prescribed trace and the outer-boundary
bound give the same envelope by scaled Dirichlet estimates.
The annuli have fixed shape, avoid the other holes, and have uniformly
small scaled old potential; their constants are independent of the
number of holes and the radius ratios.

At $\Sigma$, separated-source estimates bound the normal trace by
$C_{\rm old}q_g$ in the needed fixed norms. Correct it using
$(D_N^{\Sigma}-T)^{-1}$ and the old-boundary Poisson operator.
The correction is $O(C_{\rm old}q_g)$ on the new region and fixed old
collars, and has zero new trace. Boundary and interior Schauder
estimates on the stated patches give the scaled local bounds, since
the envelope varies by only a fixed factor there. This also proves the
fixed old-collar estimate.

label: old:product-dtn
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For an isolated sphere, the exterior harmonic Poisson extension
$P_i^{\rm harm}$, vanishing at infinity, has degree-$\ell$ radial factor
$(\rho_i/R_i)^{\ell+2a}$. Let $K$ be its off-diagonal trace matrix and
$M$ its off-diagonal normalized normal matrix. The trace on the $j$th
sphere is bounded in scaled $C^{2,\theta}$ by
$$
 C B_i\rho_i^{2a}|y_j-y_i|^{-2a}
       \|g_i/B_i\|_{C^{2,\theta}},
$$
since each scaled derivative contributes a factor
$\rho_j/|y_j-y_i|\leq\nu$. Summing by rows using \eqref{old:rows} gives
$$
 \|K\|_{\mathcal B\to\mathcal B}
 +\|M\|_{\mathcal B\to\mathcal B_1}\leq C\nu^{2a}.
$$
For small universal $\nu$, a Neumann series constructs the simultaneous
harmonic lift $P_Lg$. With $\mathcal D_0=\operatorname{diag}(\mathcal D)$,
its normal operator is
$$
 (\mathcal D_0+M)(I+K)^{-1}
 =\mathcal D_0+(M-\mathcal D_0K)(I+K)^{-1}
 =\mathcal D_0+O(\nu^{2a})
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal L(\mathcal B,\mathcal B_1).
$$
This includes reflected contributions to the diagonal.

Put $b_j=\|g_j\|_{C^{2,\theta}}$ and
$$
 E_g(x)=\sum_j\frac{b_j\rho_j^{2a}}
                    {(\rho_j^2+|x-y_j|^2)^a}.
$$
The harmonic monopoles dominate $|g|$ on every new sphere, so the
maximum principle for the harmonic lift gives $|P_Lg|\leq CE_g$.
Each summand is a positive Newton potential, and
$$
 \int_D E_g\,\mathrm d x\leq C_{\rm old}q_g.
$$
On every doubled $i$th collar, \eqref{old:rows} gives
$E_g\leq CB_i\|g\|_{\mathcal B}$; harmonic boundary estimates give the
same bound for the scaled jets of $P_Lg$.

The difference $z=P_Ng-P_Lg$ has zero new trace and satisfies
$L_0z=-V_0P_Lg$, with old interface forcing
$T(P_Lg|_\Sigma)-\partial_{\mathbf n}P_Lg$.
The forcing and the source away from a fixed new neighborhood have
fixed norms $O(C_{\rm old}q_g)$, hence responses of that size by the old
interface estimate and \eqref{old:regular-source}.
For the localized source, use \eqref{old:green-kernel} only when both
source and observation lie in that neighborhood. The 3G estimate
\eqref{pot:3Goperator} gives
$$
 \mathcal I_2(\mathbf1_{B(x,L)}E_g)(x)\leq CL^2E_g(x).
$$
Splitting the localized kernel integral at $B(x,L)$, and using the
mass bound for the far part and bounded kernel remainder, yields
$$
 |z(x)|\leq C_{\rm old}L^2E_g(x)+C_{\rm old}(L)q_g
$$
on all doubled new collars. With $\nu$ fixed, first choose $L$ small
and then $Q$ small, using
$q_g\leq C\nu^{2a}Q\|g\|_{\mathcal B}$ and $B_i\geq m_{\rm old}$.
This makes $|z|/B_i$ arbitrarily small simultaneously on every collar.
Finally decrease the largest original radius so that
$\rho_i^2V_0P_Lg/B_i$ is small in scaled $C^{0,\theta}$.
Zero-trace boundary Schauder estimates give
$$
 \|\rho_i\partial_{R_i}z/B_i\|_{C^{1,\theta}}
       \leq\varepsilon\|g\|_{\mathcal B},
$$
proving \eqref{old:dtn-comparison}. All constants in the harmonic
comparison and the rescaled collar estimates are independent of the
number of holes and their radius ratios; the old-dependent choices
are made only after $\nu$ is fixed.

label: ext:structural
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Weighted inverse estimates

title: Proof
body_md:
First use the localized kernel of Proposition~\ref{old:inverse} for source
and observation in $U_2$. For a $\Psi_i$ majorant apply
\eqref{eq:refined-source}. The singular part is at most
$C\delta\Psi_i+C_0b^2U_0$. The smooth part of the kernel is bounded
by \eqref{eq:source-masses}. For $\Phi$, split the multiplier source
into its $h$ and $bU_0$ parts. For the residual, the high--low
splitting used in \eqref{eq:source-masses} gives on $D_N$
$$
 \mathcal R_{\mathbf p}\leq Ch^p+C_0h\mathbf1_{\{h<U_0\}},\qquad
 \mathcal I_2(\mathbf1_{D_N}\mathcal R_{\mathbf p})
       \leq C\delta h+C_0b^2U_0.
$$
The residual source in the Newton potential is extended by zero
outside $D_N$.
The low-region term has bounded height and mass $O(C_0Q)$;
\eqref{eq:height-mass} and $\min_DU_0>0$ give its stated response.
Dividing the residual response by $\Phi=h+bU_0$ gives
$C\delta+C_0b$. Dividing the height--mass response
$C_0b^2U_0$ by the positive background term $bU_0$ gives $C_0b$; the
$bU_0$ multiplier part contributes at most $C\delta+C_0b^2$.
The smooth source mass contributes $C_0Q/b$. Thus both the multiplier
and the residual have coarse value bound at most
$$
 C\delta+C_0\left(b+b^2+\frac{Q}{b}\right).
$$
The old-dependent terms vanish with $Q$, since $Q/b=Q^{1-1/n}$.

Apply the kernel only to $\chi F$. Outside $U_2$, separation bounds the
response by $C_0\int|F|$.
Put $F_V=V_{\mathbf p}f$ and $F_R=\mathcal R_{\mathbf p}$. On the fixed support of
$1-\chi$, all bubbles and their ordinary jets are $O(C_0Q)$.
Require $b\leq1$ and $Q\leq b$. There $W=O(C_0b_W)$,
and hence
$$
 \left\lVert(1-\chi)F_V\right\rVert_{C^{0,\theta}}
       \leq C_0Qb_W\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{X_W},\qquad
 \left\lVert(1-\chi)F_R\right\rVert_{C^{0,\theta}}\leq C_0Q.
$$
These products extend by zero across all the new balls.
Apply \eqref{old:regular-source} to these two regular sources.
The old inverse bounds their no-hole responses by
$C_0Qb_W\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{X_W}$ and $C_0Q$, respectively, in fixed
$C^{2,\theta}$ norms on the core and old collars.
Since $B_i\geq m_{\rm old}>0$, the new-sphere traces have the same
bounds in $\mathcal B$. Applying \eqref{old:poisson-X} with the
particular weight $W=\Phi$ or $\Psi_i$, and dividing the old-collar
estimates by $A_0b_W$, gives
\begin{align*}
 \left\lVertG_N((1-\chi)V_{\mathbf p}f)\right\rVert_{X_W}
       &\leq C_0Q\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{X_W},\\
 \left\lVertG_N((1-\chi)\mathcal R_{\mathbf p})\right\rVert_{X_W}
       &\leq C_0Q/b_W.
\end{align*}
For prescribed $\varepsilon_0>0$, reduce $Q$ so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-budget}
 C_0\left(b+b^2+\frac{Q}{b}\right)
       \leq\varepsilon_0\delta.
\end{equation}
Since $b=Q^{1/n}\to0$ and $Q/b=Q^{1-1/n}\to0$, this closes
\eqref{eq:structural}, including the old-collar terms in the weighted norms. In particular,
the coefficient of $\delta$ in these estimates is universal; the
old-dependent constants are absorbed by reducing $Q$ after $\eta$
has been fixed.

For the scaled local norm apply boundary or interior Schauder
estimates after rescaling the patches. After the old data and $\eta$
are fixed, choose $r_0$ small enough that, on every new boundary
or interior patch $P$ of scale $\ell_P$,
$$
 \ell_P^2\left\lVert\kappa pU_0^q\right\rVert_{C^{0,\theta}_{\mathrm{sc}}(P)}
       \leq\delta,
$$
and the finite-order scaled relative jets of $U_0$ and the weights
$W$ needed here have universal bounds. These choices are possible
because $U_0$ is positive and smooth on the fixed core neighborhood;
the regularized potentials $h_j$ have uniformly bounded scaled relative jets.
The new potential is bounded by \eqref{eq:V-local}. For the residual source H\"older norm, use $\mathcal R_{\mathbf p}/W\leq C S_{\mathbf p}^q$,
\eqref{eq:R-jets}, and \eqref{eq:h-local}. At fixed old collars apply the separated
mass estimate and \eqref{old:regular-source}. The ordinary old-collar estimates are divided by $A_0b_W$.
Fix $A_0\geq1$ before imposing the final radius and coefficient bounds;
then reduce $Q$ so these terms obey the same inequalities.

For \eqref{eq:interface-weighted-bound}, let $w_0$ be the
smooth no-hole solution with old-interface forcing $\xi$.
The identity \eqref{old:regular-source} applies equally to this
forcing. Since $\|w_0\|_{C^{2,\theta}(D)}+
\|w_0|_{\Gamma_N}\|_{\mathcal B}\le C_0\|\xi\|_{C^{1,\theta}}$,
\eqref{old:poisson-X}, the lower bound $W\ge b_WU_0$, and the
old-collar estimates prove the claim.

Write $\mathcal I_{2,D}f=\mathcal I_2(\mathbf1_D f)$ for the Newton
potential of $f$ extended by zero outside $D$.
Finally, $U_0$ and all $h_i$ are positive Newton potentials. The 3G
inequality therefore gives $\mathcal I_{2,D}W\leq C\operatorname{diam}(D)^2W$. Its mass on $D$ is bounded by an old-dependent multiple of $b_W+Q$.
The same patch and collar argument proves bounded multiplication.
By \eqref{eq:bubble-tangents} the residual derivative has an
additional factor $\delta$: its regular coarse response is at most
$C_0\delta Q/b\leq\varepsilon_0\delta^2$, and its refined
response is at most $C_0\delta Q$. The same additional factor applies to the differentiated multiplier,
proving \eqref{eq:structural-derivatives}. No parameter-dependent
weights or domains are differentiated.

label: ext:family
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Exterior existence and Cauchy estimates

label: eq:N-multiplier
title: Proof
body_md:
On the intersection ball, $|w|\leq C\delta\Phi$ and
$b$ is small, so $|w|/S_{\mathbf p}<1/2$. Smooth Taylor formula gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:N-multiplier}
 |D_wN_{\mathbf p}(w)|\leq C|w|S_{\mathbf p}^{q-1}
 \leq C\delta V_{\mathbf p}+C_0\delta b.
\end{equation}
For the last inequality split at $h=U_0$; equivalently use
$hS_{\mathbf p}^{q-1}\leq C(S_{\mathbf p}^q-U_0^q)$ and
$U_0S_{\mathbf p}^{q-1}\leq C((S_{\mathbf p}^q-U_0^q)+U_0^q)$.
Lemma~\ref{ext:structural} controls the first term. The second term
is $b$ times a fixed old smooth multiplier, so its inverse response
has norm at most $C_0\delta b$. Thus it imposes a condition on $Q$,
without imposing an old-dependent restriction on $\eta$.
For the scaled H\"older multiplier bound, on a patch $P$ write
$D_wN=\kappa pS_{\mathbf p}^q((1+w/S_{\mathbf p})^q-1)$. The relative jets of $S_{\mathbf p}$ and
$\Phi$, and the coarse local jets of $w$, give
$$
 \left\lVertD_wN\right\rVert_{C^{0,\theta}_{\mathrm{sc}}(P)}
 \leq C\delta\Phi(x_P)S_{\mathbf p}(x_P)^{q-1}
 \leq C\delta\bigl(V_{\mathbf p}(x_P)+b U_0(x_P)^q\bigr).
$$
Multiplying by the local jets of $f$ and using the same positive
envelopes as in Lemma~\ref{ext:structural} therefore gives
$\left\lVertG_N(D_wN f)\right\rVert_{X_W}
\leq[C\delta(C\delta+o_0(1))+C_0\delta b]\left\lVertf\right\rVert_{X_W}$.
On fixed old collars the extra constants carry $b$, hence shrink with $Q$.
Also
$\left\lVert\gamma\right\rVert_{C^{2,\theta}}\leq
C_0(Q+A_0\delta b)$. Reducing $Q$ makes the old graph derivative small. Equation~\eqref{eq:interface-weighted-bound} yields, for the nonlinear
boundary contribution,
$$
 \|G_N[0,D\mathcal E(\gamma)(f|_\Sigma)]\|_{X_W}
 \leq C_0A_0\|\gamma\|_{C^{2,\theta}(\Sigma)}\|f\|_{X_W}.
$$
The affine interface forcing has size $O(C_0Q)$, and hence coarse
inverse norm $O(C_0Q/b)$. The quadratic graph term has coarse inverse
norm at most $C_0(Q+A_0\delta b)^2/b$. With $\eta,A_0$ fixed, both
are made as small as required by reducing $Q$. The refined estimates
have no factor $1/b$.

The preceding bounds show that the fixed-point map preserves a
$C\delta$ ball in $X^0$ and has derivative in $v$ of norm less than
$1/4$, so Banach's theorem gives a unique solution. The intersection
ball controls the old trace; at the solution the same contraction
bound holds on every individual $X_W$.

For each fixed finite configuration, the domain and weights are fixed,
and the weighted norms are equivalent to ordinary H\"older norms,
with configuration-dependent constants. The $C^1$ inner data from
Proposition~\ref{in:family}, the $C^2$ old graph, and the smooth power
nonlinearity in the positive neighborhood permit the implicit function
theorem, giving $C^1$ dependence on $\mathbf p$ in $X^0$. The norm equivalences
provide no uniform constants; the uniform derivative estimates follow
by differentiating \eqref{eq:exterior-fixedpoint}.
Keep $\dot P$ explicit with the orders in \eqref{eq:P-estimates}; it is
not of order $\delta$ in every refined space.
Its force $V_{\mathbf p}\dot P$ has coarse order $\delta\nu^{2a}$ and refined
order $\delta$. The derivatives of $\mathcal R_{\mathbf p},V_{\mathbf p}$ have the
extra factor $\delta$ in \eqref{eq:bubble-tangents}.

To differentiate the Taylor remainder, write
$N(S,w)=w^2 S^{q-1}F(w/S)$ and
$N_S(S,w)=w^2 S^{q-2}F_1(w/S)$, with smooth $F,F_1$ for $|w/S|<1/2$.
The scaled jets of $w$ are bounded simultaneously by
$\mathfrak A_c=C\delta\Phi$ and $\mathfrak A_i=Ck\Psi_i$; hence for $\mathfrak A_W=\mathfrak A_c$ or $\mathfrak A_i$,
$$
 \left\lVertN_S\dot S\right\rVert_{C^{0,\theta}_{\mathrm{sc}}}
 \leq C\delta h\mathfrak A_c\mathfrak A_W S^{q-2}
 \leq C\delta^2 V_{\mathbf p}\mathfrak A_W.
$$
These positive amplitude bounds also control the scaled jets.
For the old derivative terms put $\zeta_{\rm old}=Q/b$.
A unit parameter tangent has affine old forcing of ordinary size
$C_0\delta Q$, whose coarse inverse response is
$C_0\delta\zeta_{\rm old}\leq\varepsilon_0\delta^2$ by
\eqref{eq:regular-budget}. Moreover,
$$
 \left\lVert\gamma\right\rVert_{C^{2,\theta}}\leq C_0(Q+A_0\delta b),\qquad
 \left\lVert\textstyle\sum_i\dot b_i^{\mathbf p}+\dot P\right\rVert_{\rm old}
       \leq C_0(\delta+\nu^{2a})Q.
$$
The part of $D\mathcal E(\gamma)$ containing these explicit
tangents consequently has coarse response at most
$$
 C_0(Q+A_0\delta b)(\delta+\nu^{2a})\zeta_{\rm old}.
$$
After \eqref{eq:regular-budget}, further reducing $Q$ makes this
at most $\varepsilon_0(\delta^2+\delta\nu^{2a})$. The part containing $\dot v$ is included in the linearized
fixed-point operator; its norm
is at most $C_0A_0(Q+A_0\delta b)$, which can be made less than
$1/16$. Also require $C_0b\leq\varepsilon_0$ for the old bounded
multiplier term. All these conditions are compatible with fixed
$\eta,A_0,r_0$, since $b,\zeta_{\rm old}\to0$. In the refined
spaces the factors $1/b$ are absent, and the same explicit sources
are $O(\delta)$. Inverting this linearization in each $X_W$
proves \eqref{eq:v-estimates}. Boundary Schauder estimates with zero
new trace prove \eqref{eq:exterior-Cauchy}.

Finally let $J$ be a current exterior Jacobi field with radial
coefficient vector in $\mathcal W'$, physical remainder decaying at rate
$d_-$ on every eliminated old tail, and zero full trace on the new
spheres. For fixed $N$ it has finite $X_W$ norms on the core.
The lower-weight tail uniqueness in Proposition~\ref{old:graph} gives the
exact linearized old boundary relation. It follows that
$J=D_v\mathcal T(v)J$, where $\mathcal T$ is the right side of
\eqref{eq:exterior-fixedpoint}. The contraction estimate forces $J=0$.

title: Proof
body_md:

bounded inverse $C^{1,\theta}\to C^{2,\theta}$ by the standard

head: environment

label: match:estimate
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The own transformed bubbles cancel. The Cauchy-data formulas of
Section~\ref{in:section} give trace/flux pairs $(B,0)$ for a $b$
variation and $(2aB,2aB+O(\delta B))\dot{\mathbf c}\cdot\omega$
for a special conformal variation at zero. Combining these with
the exterior eigenvalues $-(\ell+2a)$ and the interior high-mode
eigenvalues $\ell$ gives the three blocks of
\eqref{eq:leading-matching}, with error $O(\delta)$.

At the baseline, Taylor-expand
$U_0+\sum_{j\ne i}b_{\lambda_j,y_j}$ at $y_i$.
Its constant term is $B_i$ and its gradient agrees with
$2aB_i\mathbf a_i^0$. The second-order error on the cutoff sphere
is $O(\nu^2B_i)$ by \eqref{pot:backgroundjets}. The change in
other bubbles caused by \eqref{eq:transformed-bubble} is
$O(\eta^2B_i)$ at the baseline and $O(\delta B_i)$ for unit
tangents. For $V_B$, the boundary data and radial equation bound the required
nonconstant jets and their first parameter derivatives on a two-sided
annulus by $O(\delta B)$.
Taylor expansion in $|\mathbf a_i|\rho_i=O(\nu+Rk)$ gives the
low-mode derivative error $O(\nu+\delta+Rk)$.

Proposition~\ref{in:family} bounds the normalized Cauchy-data
contribution of the inner correction and its parameter derivative by
$O_R(\nu+s^{2-\mu_3})$. Indeed, the fixed gap
$d=\mu_3-\mu_2>0$ gives
$$
 (1+\log(1/s))s^{2-\mu_2}
 =s^{2-\mu_3}(1+\log(1/s))s^d
 \leq C_d s^{2-\mu_3},
$$
while $\nu^aRk\leq2R\nu$ since $k\leq2\nu^2$ and $\nu\leq1$.
Proposition~\ref{old:product-dtn} gives the
full exterior Poisson flux as its diagonal harmonic operator plus
$O(\nu^{2a})+o_0(1)$. The derivatives of the boundary discrepancy $g_i$, after the own
bubble cancellation, are bounded in the $B_i$-normalized norm by
\eqref{eq:g-estimates}.
The zero-trace nonlinear correction has flux error $O(\delta)$ by
\eqref{eq:exterior-Cauchy}. Since $n\geq3$ and $\nu\leq1$,
$\delta=\nu^n\leq\nu$, $\nu^{2a}=\nu^{n-2}\leq\nu$, and
$Rk\leq2R\nu$. Thus all the universal derivative errors are absorbed
in $C_R(\nu+s^{2-\mu_3})$, proving the derivative estimate.

At $\mathbf p=0$ the high data and its correction vanish. The exterior
correction is bounded by its force times $(1-1/4)^{-1}$, independently
of the parameter-ball radius. Its flux and the Taylor errors therefore
give $C_*$ independently of $R$.

label: match:inner-kernel
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{match:inner-kernel}
Let $I=\mathcal T_{\mathbf a}U_B+Z$ be an inner solution above, with
$Z\in C^{2,\theta}_{\mu_3}$. Every additive Jacobi field $J$ for $I$
that belongs to $C^{2,\theta}(\overline{B_\rho}\setminus B_{\rho'})$
for every $0<\rho'<\rho$, and whose relative factor $J/I$ is $O(r^d)$ at the puncture for some
$d>0$ is a linear combination of the special conformal and
high-boundary-data tangents of $I$, with $A$ and $B$ fixed. Constants in this representation may depend
on the fixed positive neck.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The assumed regularity gives a $C^{2,\theta}$ boundary trace.
Since $I\asymp r^{-a}$ for the fixed positive neck, the relative
bound implies $J=O(r^{-a+d})$. Annular Schauder estimates for the
Jacobi equation give the corresponding scaled derivative bounds. Write $U=\mathcal T_{\mathbf a}U_B$.
For a positive conformal factor $f$, write $L_f=\Delta+\kappa p f^q$
for its additive Jacobi operator, as in \eqref{in:inverse}.
Undo the special conformal transformation on a smaller concentric ball
in the transformed domain. The pullback fixes the origin, has comparable
radial variables and a smooth nonvanishing conformal factor, and
preserves the strong additive weights.
On this ball the transformed solution and Jacobi field satisfy
$$
 \widetilde I=U_B+\widetilde Z,
 \qquad \widetilde Z\in C^{2,\theta}_{\mu_3},
 \qquad \widetilde J=O(r^{-a+d}),
$$
with scaled derivatives. In the following argument $\varepsilon>0$
denotes the fixed necksize, and $d>0$ denotes the decay exponent of
the field. Since $U_B\asymp r^{-a}$,
Taylor expansion gives
$$
 (L_{\widetilde I}-L_{U_B})\widetilde J
               =O(r^{\mu_3+d-2}).
$$
Set $j=r^a\widetilde J$ and $t=-\log r$ (up to an additive constant).
The radial cylindrical Jacobi equation is
$$
 P_\varepsilon j=f,\qquad
 P_\varepsilon=\partial_t^2+\Delta_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}
                   -a^2+\kappa p v^q,
 \qquad f=O(e^{-(a+\mu_3+d)t}),
$$
where $v=r^aU_B$ is a phase translate of the Fowler profile.
Since $\kappa p=n(n+2)/4$, this is the cylindrical normalization of
\cite[Section~2.2]{KMPS1999}.
Initially $j\in \mathcal C_{d_0}^{2,\theta}$ on the cylinder for any
$0<d_0<\min\{d,1\}$.

Choose $\gamma=a+\mu_1$, so $\gamma>1$ and $\gamma<a+2$.
By Lemma~2 of \cite[Section~5]{MP1999}, the first high-mode indicial
exponent $\gamma_{\varepsilon,n+1}$ has a lower bound arbitrarily close
to $a+2$ for small necks. Reducing the small-neck threshold in terms
of $n$ and $\mu_1$ gives $\gamma_{\varepsilon,n+1}>\gamma$. Since
$a+\mu_3+d>\gamma$, Corollary~1 of
\cite[Section~2.2]{KMPS1999} applies and gives
$$
 j\in \mathcal C_{\gamma}^{2,\theta}\oplus E_{\varepsilon,1}.
$$
Here $E_{\varepsilon,1}$ is the span of the stable first spherical
Jacobi fields. In additive Euclidean variables these are precisely
the fixed-center special conformal generators,
$r^{1-a}(av-v')\omega_j$. Hence $\widetilde J$ is a combination of
these generators plus a field in $X_{\mu_1}$. The initial positive decay excludes the two neutral radial fields
and the growing first-degree fields. The weight conversion is
$j\in \mathcal C_{\gamma}^{2,\theta}\Longleftrightarrow
\widetilde J\in X_{\gamma-a}$; with $\gamma=a+\mu_1$, the remainder
therefore belongs to $X_{\mu_1}$. All norms are finite on the remaining compact annulus.

Return through the conformal transformation. The special conformal
transformations satisfy the local group law
$\mathcal T_{\mathbf a+\mathbf z}
=\mathcal T_{\mathbf a}\mathcal T_{\mathbf z}$.
Consequently their parameter tangents have precisely the stable
first-degree leading terms found above.
Proposition~\ref{in:family} places the derivatives of the correction
in $X_{\mu_3}$. Subtracting suitable special conformal tangents of
$I$ therefore leaves a field in $X_{\mu_1}$, with positive relative
decay. Choose $\dot\psi$ so that
$B_*\dot\psi$ equals the remaining high trace, and subtract the
corresponding high-boundary tangent of $I$, which belongs to $X_{\mu_3}$.
The remainder $J_0$ is a strong Jacobi field with zero high trace.
The local strong inverse gives
$$
 J_0=-G_U\bigl[(L_I-L_U)J_0\bigr].
$$
The operator on the right has norm less than one on $X_{\mu_1}$ by the
small relative potential estimate, so $J_0=0$.

label: match:nondegenerate
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{match:nondegenerate}
The matched finite-ended metric is marked nondegenerate.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $J$ be a global marked Jacobi field. Its smoothness at the matching
spheres allows Lemma~\ref{match:inner-kernel} to represent it at every
new puncture as an inner tangent with $\dot b_i=0$. Passing from physical coefficients
to \eqref{eq:parameter-space} multiplies the special conformal
coefficient by $\rho_i$ and divides the high trace by $B_i$.
Since these finitely many factors are positive, this defines
$\dot{\mathbf p}\in\mathcal E_N$. No uniform bound on the representation coefficients
is needed for this kernel argument.

At each old end the radial coefficients of a marked field are zero.
It therefore satisfies the current common gauge and the lower-weight
boundary graph of Proposition~\ref{old:graph}. Because $E_{\mathbf p}|_{\Gamma_i}=I_i(\mathbf p)|_{\Gamma_i}$ for all parameters,
$D_{\mathbf p}E_{\mathbf p}[\dot{\mathbf p}]$ has exactly the same full new trace as $J$.
The old radial coefficient vector of this exterior tangent belongs to
$\mathcal W'$, and its physical remainder has decay $d_-$ by
Proposition~\ref{old:graph}. Since the old radial coefficients of $J$
vanish, their difference belongs to the same current Jacobi space
and has zero full trace on the new spheres. Exterior uniqueness in
Lemma~\ref{ext:family} therefore makes it zero. The vanishing global
normal jump then says $D\mathcal M\dot{\mathbf p}=0$. The bound in
\eqref{eq:mismatch-estimates} makes $D\mathcal M$ invertible; hence
$\dot{\mathbf p}=0$, and all restrictions of $J$ vanish.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The preceding matching argument and
Proposition~\ref{match:nondegenerate} give a smooth positive
marked nondegenerate solution. It remains to verify the uniform
order of choices, lower bound, and approximation statements.

Fix
the universal data, the three weights, and the parameter-ball radius
$R$ determined above. Choose $\eta_*$ from the local inverse thresholds, the high-mode
indicial bound in Lemma~\ref{match:inner-kernel},
inner Cauchy estimates, exterior contraction, and matching estimates.
Decrease $\eta_*$ so that $\eta_*\leq1$ and
$\eta_*^{2/(n+2)}<1/4$.
Fix $\eta\leq\eta_*$, then choose the old cuts, the regular infinity
cap, the two old weights, the common complement, and the old inverse
constants. Choose the fixed buffers, $r_0$, and $A_0$ next.
Reduce the maximal radius to meet the old jet bounds and
the localized Poisson comparison estimates, and impose
$10r_{\max}<\operatorname{dist}(K,\partial D_{\rm pre})$ on the prescribed core.
If $K$ is empty, only the trivial empty insertion is needed. Finally reduce $Q$ to
meet the old spectral, boundary-graph, and smoothing estimates.
The choices are compatible: $b=Q^{1/n}\to0$ and
$Q/b=Q^{1-1/n}\to0$, while the capacity estimate at the end of
Section~\ref{old:section} gives $\sum_i\rho_i^{2a}\to0$.
On the core the matched factor is $S_{\mathbf p}+P+v$ and
$|P+v|\leq C\delta(h+b U_0)$. The transformed bubbles are
uniformly comparable with $h_i$, and $S_{\mathbf p}\asymp U_0+h$.
For small universal $\delta$ and small old-dependent $b$ this
gives \eqref{eq:core-lower}. The own term gives
\eqref{eq:shell-lower}. The inner estimates imply complete,
positive, noncylindrical new ends; the old graph preserves the old
positive necks.

On a protected compact set disjoint from the new centers, all bubble
jets are $O(Q)$, and the correction bounded by $C\delta\Phi$ tends to zero with $b$.
Elliptic bootstrap gives convergence in every prescribed finite
smoothness norm. On an old tail the compact set occupies a finite
cylindrical interval, where the period-aligned family is continuous
in these norms. The compact Dirichlet implicit function theorem gives
the same conclusion on the regular cap.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $\dim_{\mathrm H}\Lambda<\beta<a$, fix the packing constant
from Lemma~\ref{pot:cover}, and fix
$0<\eta\leq\min\{\eta_*,1\}$. Denote by $c_0\in(0,1]$ and $c_1>0$
the constants in \eqref{eq:core-lower} and \eqref{eq:shell-lower},
respectively. All constants in the length estimates below are
independent of the step.

Start with a noncylindrical Delaunay metric with singularities at two
chosen points of $\Lambda$, transported by a conformal automorphism
of the sphere. This metric is marked nondegenerate: its radial Jacobi
fields are neutral, the first spherical modes grow at one end, and
the higher modes are coercive; see \cite[Section~II, Lemma~2.21]{MPU1996}
and \cite[Section~II]{MPU1995}. If $\Lambda$ is finite, insert its
remaining points by successive single-ball applications of the finite
gluing statement. The resulting finite-ended metric is complete,
and Lemma~\ref{pot:oldrepresentation} gives the asserted integrability
and global equation. Henceforth assume that $\Lambda$ is infinite.

Fix a stereographic pole outside $\Lambda$. All balls used in the
construction are Euclidean balls in this chart, whereas
$N_\sigma(\Lambda)$ denotes a round-metric neighborhood. Choose a
compact exhaustion $L_j\Subset\Omega$ with
$L_j\subset\operatorname{int}L_{j+1}$, and choose $\epsilon_j\in(0,1)$
so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:product-budget}
 \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\epsilon_j<\frac14.
\end{equation}
Thus every finite or infinite product of factors $1-\epsilon_j$ is
greater than $3/4$.

Suppose that $g_{j-1}=u_{j-1}^{2/a}g_{\mathrm{rd}}$ is a marked
nondegenerate finite-ended solution with singular set
$F_{j-1}\subset\Lambda$, and that compact sets
$W_1,\ldots,W_{j-1}\Subset\Omega$ have been constructed. Choose
$\sigma_j<2^{-j}$, decreasing with $j$, so that
$\overline{N_{\sigma_j}(\Lambda)}$ misses
$L_j\cup\bigcup_{\ell<j}W_\ell$.

For every $z\in F_{j-1}$, choose an outer radius $b_z$ such that the
closed balls $\overline{B(z,b_z)}$ are pairwise disjoint, lie in
$N_{\sigma_j}(\Lambda)$, and satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:old-end-bound}
 U_{j-1}(x)\geq m_z|x-z|^{-a}
 \qquad (0<|x-z|\leq b_z)
\end{equation}
for some $m_z>0$. This follows from the positive Delaunay profile of
each end. Choose $a_z\in(0,b_z)$ and a smooth logarithmic cutoff
$f_z$, equal to one for $|x-z|\leq a_z$ and zero for
$|x-z|\geq b_z$, with
$$
 |D f_z|\leq\frac{C}{|x-z|\log(b_z/a_z)}.
$$
By decreasing $a_z$, arrange
\begin{equation}\label{eq:old-cutoff-gradient}
 |\mathrm d f_z|_{g_{j-1}}\leq\frac{c_0^{1/a}}{\eta}
 \qquad\text{on the transition annulus}.
\end{equation}
Indeed, \eqref{eq:old-end-bound} bounds this gradient by
$C/(m_z^{1/a}\log(b_z/a_z))$.

Choose the old end sections strictly inside $B(z,a_z/2)$, and choose
the regular cap at the stereographic pole away from the logarithmic
annuli and the compact set
$$
 E_j=\Lambda\setminus\bigcup_{z\in F_{j-1}}B(z,a_z).
$$
The resulting truncated core contains these annuli and $E_j$ in its
interior. Specify $K=E_j$ before selecting the radius and coefficient
bounds in the finite gluing statement.

Since $\mathcal H^\beta(E_j)=0$, Lemma~\ref{pot:cover} gives finitely many
disjoint balls $B(y_i,r_i)$, with centers $y_i\in E_j$, whose
open fivefold enlargements cover $E_j$. Their tenfold enlargements
can be required to lie in the interior of the old core and in
$N_{\sigma_j}(\Lambda)$. Their maximum radius and total $\beta$-cost
can be made arbitrarily small. Equation~\eqref{pot:charge}
therefore makes $Q$ satisfy all prescribed coefficient bounds.

Apply the finite gluing statement, requiring in addition that
\begin{align}
 \|u_j-u_{j-1}\|_{C^j(L_j)}&\leq2^{-j},
       \label{eq:absolute-budget}\\
 |u_j-u_{j-1}|&\leq\epsilon_j u_{j-1}
       &&\text{on }L_j\cup\bigcup_{\ell<j}W_\ell.
       \label{eq:relative-budget}
\end{align}
These are finitely many compact approximation requirements; the
relative bounds are possible because $u_{j-1}$ has a positive minimum
on each protected compact set. The output has singular set
$F_j=F_{j-1}\cup\{y_i\}$ and remains marked nondegenerate with
noncylindrical ends. If $E_j=\varnothing$, take $u_j=u_{j-1}$.
By Lemma~\ref{pot:oldrepresentation}, every finite-step factor $u_j$
belongs to $L^p(\mathbb S^n)$ and satisfies the global distributional
equation.

For every new ball choose a smooth cutoff $\chi_i$, equal to one on
$B(y_i,5r_i)$ and zero outside $B(y_i,10r_i)$, with $|D\chi_i|\leq C/r_i$.
Extend all the cutoffs smoothly over the sphere, and set
\begin{equation}\label{eq:barrier-definition}
 f_j=\max\bigl(\{f_z:z\in F_{j-1}\}\cup\{\chi_i\}_i\bigr),
 \qquad W_j=\{1/4\leq f_j\leq3/4\}.
\end{equation}
The old inner balls and new open fivefold balls cover $\Lambda$.
Consequently, $f_j=1$ on an open neighborhood $V_j$ of $\Lambda$,
and both $\mathbb S^n\setminus V_j$ and $W_j$ are compact subsets of
$\Omega$. Since $\operatorname{supp} f_j\subset N_{\sigma_j}(\Lambda)$, the later
supports miss $W_j$; hence the sets $W_j$ are pairwise disjoint.

At a point of $W_j$, every new fivefold ball is avoided. If a new
cutoff $\chi_i$ is active in the maximum, its point lies in $B(y_i,10r_i)$,
and \eqref{eq:shell-lower} gives
$$
 U_j^{1/a}\geq c_1^{1/a}\frac{\eta}{r_i},
 \qquad |\mathrm d\chi_i|_{g_j}\leq\frac{C}{\eta}.
$$
An active old cutoff lies in its logarithmic annulus, in the old core.
Every point of $W_j$ lies outside all the balls $B(y_i,5r_i)$,
and hence outside all the matching balls $B(y_i,\rho_i)$. Thus
\eqref{eq:core-lower} and \eqref{eq:old-cutoff-gradient} give
$|\mathrm d f_z|_{g_j}\leq1/\eta$. The same estimate holds when no new
balls are inserted. Every active cutoff on $W_j$ therefore has
metric gradient bounded by $C/\eta$.

The bounds \eqref{eq:absolute-budget} imply convergence to a smooth
function $u\geq0$ locally on $\Omega$: for any fixed $m,k$, the
$C^k(L_m)$ tail is summable. Passing to the local equations yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:local-limit-equation}
 \mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}u=\kappa u^p\qquad\text{on }\Omega.
\end{equation}
For $x\in L_m$, \eqref{eq:relative-budget} gives
$$
 u(x)\geq u_m(x)\prod_{j>m}(1-\epsilon_j)>0.
$$
Hence $g=u^{2/a}g_{\mathrm{rd}}$ is a smooth metric with scalar
curvature $n(n-1)$. The same product estimate on the protected sets
gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:protected-limit}
 u\geq\frac34u_j\qquad\text{on }W_j.
\end{equation}

Each $f_j$ is the finite maximum of smooth functions and is therefore
locally Lipschitz. Along a locally absolutely continuous curve,
its derivative agrees almost everywhere with that of an active
cutoff. Together with \eqref{eq:protected-limit}, the gradient
estimates give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:curve-cutoff}
 |(f_j\circ\gamma)'(t)|
 \leq\frac{C'}{\eta}|\dot\gamma(t)|_g
 \quad\text{for almost every }t\text{ with }\gamma(t)\in W_j,
\end{equation}
where $C'$ is independent of $j$.

Let $\gamma$ be a locally absolutely continuous curve leaving
every compact subset of $\Omega$. For every sufficiently large
$j$, its starting point is outside $\operatorname{supp} f_j$, whereas it is
eventually in $V_j$, because $\mathbb S^n\setminus V_j\Subset\Omega$.
Thus it crosses $W_j$ from level $1/4$ to level $3/4$.
Integrating \eqref{eq:curve-cutoff} gives
$$
 \int_{\gamma^{-1}(W_j)}|\dot\gamma(t)|_g\,\mathrm d t
       \ge\frac{\eta}{2C'}.
$$
The $W_j$ are pairwise disjoint, so every such curve has infinite
length. The divergent-curve criterion for Riemannian completeness
therefore proves that $g$ is complete.
Finally, $\mathcal H^a(\Lambda)=0$, so Proposition~\ref{prop:no-defect}
below gives the global equation and the asserted $L^p$ integrability.
head: environment

label: prop:no-defect
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:no-defect}
Let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb S^n$ be closed, with $\mathcal H^a(\Lambda)=0$.
Suppose that $u_j>0$ belong to $L^p(\mathbb S^n)$, satisfy
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}u_j=\kappa u_j^p$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb S^n)$, and converge smoothly
locally on $\mathbb S^n\setminus\Lambda$ to $u$. Then
$$
 u_j^p\longrightarrow u^p\quad\text{in }L^1(\mathbb S^n),
 \qquad
 u_j\longrightarrow u\quad\text{in }L^p(\mathbb S^n),
$$
and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}u=\kappa u^p$ globally in distributions. Moreover, the source
measures $\mu_j=\kappa u_j^p\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:source-morrey}
 \mu_j(B_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}(x,r))\leq C_n r^a
 \qquad(0<r\leq r_0),
\end{equation}
where $C_n,r_0>0$ depend only on $n$. In particular, no additional
limiting source measure is supported on $\Lambda$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Define $u$ arbitrarily on the measure-zero set $\Lambda$.

For the local estimate, we use the test-function method of
Mitidieri and Pohozaev; see \cite[Section~1, equations~(1.2)--(1.5)]{MitidieriPohozaev2004},
with numbering from their March 2004 manuscript. Put
$p'=p/(p-1)=(n+2)/4$ and choose an integer $m>2p'$.
For $B=B_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}(x,r)$, $0<r\leq r_0\leq1$, choose
$0\leq\psi\leq1$, equal to one on $B$, supported in $2B$, with
$|\nabla\psi|\leq C_n/r$ and $|\Delta\psi|\leq C_n/r^2$.
Then $\varphi=\psi^m$ satisfies
$$
 |\mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}\varphi|\leq C_n r^{-2}\psi^{m-2}
             \leq C_n r^{-2}\varphi^{1/p}.
$$
Writing $X_j=\int u_j^p\varphi\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}$, the equation and H\"older's
inequality give
$$
 \kappa X_j=\int u_j\mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}\varphi\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}
 \leq C_n r^{-2}X_j^{1/p}
           \operatorname{Vol}(2B)^{1/p'}.
$$
If $X_j>0$, divide by $X_j^{1/p}$ and raise to the power $p'$;
the zero case is immediate. Since $n-2p'=a$, this yields
$$
 \int_Bu_j^p\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}\leq X_j\leq C_n r^a,
$$
which proves \eqref{eq:source-morrey} in every dimension $n\geq3$.
Testing with one gives $\int u_j^p=\int u_j$; H\"older's
inequality implies $\int u_j^p\le\operatorname{Vol}(\mathbb S^n)$.
Fatou's lemma therefore yields $u\in L^p(\mathbb S^n)$.

Given $\varepsilon>0$, cover $\Lambda$ by finitely many open round
balls $B(x_i,r_i)$, with $r_i\leq r_0$ and
$\sum_i r_i^a<\varepsilon$, and let $O$ be their union.
The local estimate gives
$$
 \kappa\int_Ou_j^p\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}\leq C_n\varepsilon
 \qquad\text{for every }j,
$$
and Fatou's lemma gives the same bound for $u^p$.
On $\mathbb S^n\setminus O\Subset\mathbb S^n\setminus\Lambda$, the sources
converge uniformly. Therefore
$$
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}\kappa
 \int_{\mathbb S^n}|u_j^p-u^p|\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}\leq2C_n\varepsilon.
$$
Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ proves strong $L^1$ convergence.

For $s,t\geq0$, $|s-t|^p\leq|s^p-t^p|$, since
$(t+h)^p\geq t^p+h^p$ for $h\geq0$. Thus
$$
 \|u_j-u\|_{L^p}^p\leq\|u_j^p-u^p\|_{L^1}\longrightarrow0.
$$
The factors also converge in $L^1$, so for every
$\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb S^n)$ we can pass to the limit in
$$
 \int_{\mathbb S^n}u_j\mathcal A_{\mathrm{rd}}\varphi\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}
 =\kappa\int_{\mathbb S^n}u_j^p\varphi\,\mathrm d V_{g_{\mathrm{rd}}}.
$$
This proves the global distributional equation. Strong $L^1$
convergence of the sources excludes an additional measure on
$\Lambda$.
